text: Newborn, female. The patient is a 3000-g (6.6-lb) female newborn delivered at term to a 23-year-old primigravida mother. The mother reports having had no prenatal care, and immunization records for the newborn are not available.

speaker: Doctor
text: I have noted that the patient is a 3000g female newborn born at term, with no prenatal care and unavailable immunization records. To proceed with the evaluation, what specific physical symptoms or abnormalities did you observe upon birth or since then?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Continuous heart murmur. I also have Bluish macules on the skin that do not blanch with pressure, Cloudy lenses in both eyes noticed upon examination, Failure to pass auditory screening tests.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Rubella Syndrome. The combination of a continuous heart murmur (likely a PDA), bluish non-blanching skin macules (petechiae or purpura), cloudy lenses (congenital cataracts), and hearing loss constitutes the classic triad of symptoms associated with this infection in a newborn lacking immunization history.
